3: Normal forms for CFGs: CNF and GNF

questions.q: Design a DFA over {0, 1} that accepts exactly the strings containing an even number of 0s and ending in 1. Give the transition table and state the purpose of each state.
questions.model: Track (parity of 0s, last symbol). States: q0 = even 0s, not ending in 1 (start); q1 = even 0s, ending in 1 (accepting); q2 = odd 0s, ending in 0; q3 = odd 0s, ending in 1. On 0: q0->q2, q1->q2, q2->q0, q3->q0. On 1: q0->q1, q1->q1, q2->q3, q3->q3. Accept q1.

questions.q: Using the subset construction, what is the maximum number of states of the DFA equivalent to an NFA with 4 states?
questions.model: Each DFA state is a subset of the NFA states: at most 2^4 = 16.

questions.q: Minimise the DFA with states A (start), B, C, D, E (E accepting) over {0, 1}: A: 0->B, 1->C; B: 0->B, 1->D; C: 0->B, 1->C; D: 0->B, 1->E; E: 0->B, 1->C. Show the partitions and the number of states in the minimal DFA.
questions.model: P0 = {A,B,C,D}, {E}. On 1, D goes to E: P1 = {A,B,C}, {D}, {E}. On 1, B goes to D: P2 = {A,C}, {B}, {D}, {E}. P3 = P2 (stable). A and C merge: the minimal DFA has 4 states.

questions.q: True or False: The strings a, aa, aaa, ... are pairwise distinguishable with respect to L = {a^n b^n : n >= 0}, so by the Myhill-Nerode theorem L is not regular.
questions.model: True. a^i b^i is in L but a^j b^i is not for i != j, giving infinitely many equivalence classes, so L is not regular.

questions.q: Use the pumping lemma to prove that L = {a^n b^n : n >= 0} is not regular.
questions.model: Assume L regular with pumping length p. Take w = a^p b^p, w = xyz with |xy| <= p, |y| >= 1, so y = a^k (k >= 1). Then x y^2 z = a^(p+k) b^p is not in L, contradicting the lemma. Hence L is not regular.

questions.q: Write a regular expression for the strings over {0, 1} whose third symbol from the right end is 1, and state the minimum length of a string it accepts.
questions.model: (0+1)* 1 (0+1)(0+1); the shortest accepted strings have length 3 (e.g. 100).

questions.q: A DFA has states q1 (start and accepting) and q2 over {a, b}: q1 on a -> q1, on b -> q2; q2 on a -> q1, on b -> q2. Using Arden's theorem, derive a regular expression for its language.
questions.model: Equations: q1 = e + q1 a + q2 a; q2 = q1 b + q2 b. Arden on q2: q2 = q1 b b*. Substitute: q1 = e + q1 (a + b b* a). Arden: q1 = (a + b b* a)*. The language is the empty string and all strings ending in a.

questions.q: Regular languages are NOT closed under which of the following operations?
questions.model: Every language is an infinite union of singleton (regular) languages, so closure fails for infinite unions.

questions.q: Design a Mealy machine for the vending controller in the case, giving its states, inputs, outputs and transition table, and explain how a Moore machine for the same behaviour would differ.
questions.case: A ticket vending controller accepts Rs 5 and Rs 10 coins one at a time. When the amount inserted reaches Rs 15 it outputs a ticket (and returns Rs 5 change if Rs 20 was inserted); otherwise it outputs nothing and waits for the next coin.
questions.model: States S0, S5, S10 (amount held). Inputs 5, 10. S0: 5/none -> S5, 10/none -> S10. S5: 5/none -> S10, 10/ticket -> S0. S10: 5/ticket -> S0, 10/ticket+change -> S0. A Moore machine attaches outputs to states, so it needs extra states such as T (ticket) and TC (ticket + change), and responds one transition later.

questions.q: Show that the grammar E -> E + E | E * E | id is ambiguous using the string id + id * id, and explain why ambiguity matters for a compiler.
questions.model: Two leftmost derivations / parse trees: one groups id + (id * id), the other (id + id) * id. They give different evaluation orders, so a compiler could compute different meanings; precedence must be encoded in an unambiguous grammar.

questions.t: Normal forms for CFGs: CNF and GNF
questions.q: Convert the grammar S -> aSb | ab into Chomsky Normal Form, showing each step.
questions.model: Introduce A -> a, B -> b: S -> ASB | AB. Break ASB with X -> SB: S -> AX | AB, X -> SB, A -> a, B -> b. All rules are now A -> BC or A -> a.

questions.q: True or False: The language {a^n b^n c^n : n >= 1} is context free.
questions.model: False. The pumping lemma for CFLs shows it is not context free.

questions.q: Design a context-free grammar for all palindromes over {a, b} and draw the derivation tree for abba.
questions.model: S -> aSa | bSb | a | b | e. abba: S => aSa => abSba => abba (S -> e); the tree has root S with children a, S, a; the inner S has children b, S, b; the innermost S derives e.

questions.q: Design a PDA that accepts {a^n b^n : n >= 1} by empty stack. Give the transition function and the sequence of instantaneous descriptions for the input aabb.
questions.model: States q0, q1; bottom marker Z. d(q0, a, Z) = (q0, AZ); d(q0, a, A) = (q0, AA); d(q0, b, A) = (q1, e); d(q1, b, A) = (q1, e); d(q1, e, Z) = (q1, e). IDs: (q0, aabb, Z) |- (q0, abb, AZ) |- (q0, bb, AAZ) |- (q1, b, AZ) |- (q1, e, Z) |- (q1, e, e): accepted.

questions.q: Which of these languages cannot be accepted by any deterministic PDA?
questions.model: For w w^R the machine cannot know where the middle is without a marker; it needs nondeterminism. w c w^R has the marker c.

questions.q: Explain how a PDA accepting by empty stack is constructed from a CFG, and why it simulates leftmost derivations.
questions.model: One state; start with S on the stack. For each variable A and rule A -> x: an e-move replacing A by x on the stack. For each terminal a: read a and pop a. The stack holds the unread part of a sentential form, expanding the leftmost variable each time, so it follows a leftmost derivation.

questions.q: Read the assertion and reason about two stack PDA and choose the correct option.
questions.assertion: A PDA with two stacks is as powerful as a Turing machine.
questions.reason: The two stacks can hold the tape contents to the left and to the right of the head.
questions.model: Both true and R explains A: moving the head is popping one stack and pushing the other.

questions.q: Prove that the halting problem for Turing machines is undecidable.
questions.model: Suppose H(M, w) decides whether M halts on w. Build D(M): run H(M, M); if it says 'halts', loop forever, else halt. D(D) halts iff H(D, D) says it does not halt: contradiction. So no such H exists.

questions.q: What is a universal Turing machine, and why is it considered a model of the stored-program computer?
questions.model: A TM U that takes an encoding <M, w> and simulates M on w. Like a stored-program computer, the program (M) is data on the tape, so one machine runs any program.

questions.q: For the PCP instance A = (1, 10111, 10) and B = (111, 10, 0), find a solution sequence of indices and show that both concatenations are equal.
